rubrics.justification: Generally recognizes a blastocyst with visible ICM and TE, but overstates image quality details (e.g., uniform cohesive TE, minimal vacuolization, homogeneous cytoplasm) and is somewhat inconsistent about expansion stage versus the reported 2AA.
Integrates age, diagnosis, oocyte yield, first cycle status, BMI, sperm parameters, and especially thin endometrium with embryo quality and prognosis; AMH is unavailable but not mishandled.

Overall logic is structured, but there are notable issues: it questions the reported Gardner expansion grade, assigns specific percentage adjustments without clear basis, and infers male-factor concerns despite normal semen concentration/motility.

Appropriate support for single embryo transfer and attention to thin endometrium, but several adjunct recommendations (aspirin, G-CSF, acupuncture, embryo glue, ERA after a single failure) are not strongly guideline-supported for routine use.

Provides concrete next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including eSET and consideration of freeze-all if lining is inadequate, though some suggested interventions are more speculative than standard.
